name: logo
description:
The avenCEO lockup: the mark, the wordmark, or both. The wordmark is TWO faces in one word — "aven" in the thin display face at 1.4em, "CEO" in the heaviest sans, uppercase — a specification that used to live inline at every call site, including two `style` attributes in the site header.

It was extracted as a SHELL, and that is worth recording. The unit declared the flex container and nothing else: no parts, and three `variant` options that differed only in `gap`. Everything inside it — the mark's size, the two faces, the baseline alignment — resolved through `logo-mark`, `logo-wordmark`, `logo-word-aven` and `logo-word-ceo`, which are LEGACY classes this unit exists to replace. So the unit rendered correctly while owning none of its own appearance, and would have rendered as unstyled text the day the legacy map was deleted.

It also could not do what its variants claimed. `mark` and `wordmark` only set `gap: 0`; the only thing producing a mark-only logo was the caller omitting the wordmark from the markup. A variant that needs the caller to change the children is not a variant — it is a naming convention. The variants now HIDE the part that does not belong, so one markup and one class give all three.

base.$description: `gap: 0.625rem` is the header's own `gap-2.5`, not `--space-tight` (0.5rem). Extracting it to the nearest token would have moved the wordmark two pixels closer to the mark on every surface — a silent change to the one element nobody is allowed to change silently.

mark.$description: 1.75rem square, and it never shrinks — in a flex bar a mark that shrinks is a mark that becomes an oval.

wordmark.$description: Two faces in one word, aligned on the BASELINE rather than centred — the display 'aven' is 1.4em and centring it would leave the two halves sitting at different heights.

variant.$description: Which half is shown. These HIDE a part rather than adjusting the gap around one the caller already left out, so the same markup produces all three and a surface never has to know which children a variant expects.

mark.$description: The mark alone — a favicon, an avatar, a collapsed rail.

wordmark.$description: The word alone — inside a heading, where a mark would read as a bullet.

a11y.note: The mark is `alt=""` — decorative, because the wordmark beside it already carries the name as real text. On the `mark` variant the wordmark is `display: none` and therefore hidden from assistive tech too, so that variant's container needs its own accessible name (an `aria-label` on the link, or visually hidden text); a bare mark with an empty alt is a link with no name.
